title: Microsoft Purview DSPM: Copilot Prompt Gallery of built-in Security Copilot prompts
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, gallery behaviour, licensing prerequisites and governance controls are supported. Minor corrections should distinguish included SCU consumption from additional billing and finish the role-assignment path.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-06-25T23:15:45.
DSPM (classic) includes a gallery of built-in Security Copilot prompts.
claims.quote: Data Security Posture Management also offers built-in prompts to help you investigate sensitive areas, potentially risky users, potentially suspicious activity, and more in your organization.

claims.claim: DSPM reports on unprotected sensitive data assets and potentially risky user activities.
claims.quote: Use Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) to quickly identify unprotected sensitive data assets and potentially risky user activities in your organization.

claims.claim: In the Purview portal, open Data Security Posture Management (classic), Overview, then View more in prompt gallery under Get started with Security Copilot featured promptbooks.
claims.quote: Select the Data Security Posture Management (classic) solution card, then select Overview in the left nav. ... select View more in prompt gallery in the Get started with Security Copilot featured promptbooks section on the Overview page.

claims.claim: An analyst can customize a built-in gallery prompt or run it directly in Copilot.
claims.quote: You can customize the built-in prompt or immediately run the prompt directly in Copilot.

claims.claim: The gallery categories are Alerts and policies, Data at risk, Potentially risky users, Potentially suspicious activity, and Sensitive data.
claims.quote: Select built-in Copilot prompts from the following categories: Alerts and policies; Data at risk; Potentially risky users; Potentially suspicious activity; Sensitive data

claims.claim: The featured Risky user investigation promptbook runs six prompts in sequence.
claims.quote: This promptbook is a six-prompt sequence that helps you investigate users handling sensitive data and shows their data activities, anomalies, and related alerts.

claims.claim: The featured Sensitive data protection promptbook runs six prompts in sequence.
claims.quote: This promptbook is a sequence of six prompts that helps you identify and protect sensitive data across your organization.

claims.claim: The Sensitive data protection promptbook suggests policy changes and DLP rules.
claims.quote: It suggests recommended policy changes and data loss prevention rules.

claims.claim: DSPM Copilot insights come from scanned DLP, Information Protection and Insider Risk Management data.
claims.quote: Data security insights come from scanned data across Data Loss Prevention (DLP), Information Protection, and Insider Risk Management solutions in Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Without a specified date period, responses include only the last 10 days of data.
claims.quote: If you don't specify a date period, only data from the last 10 days from current date is included.

claims.claim: The maximum data lookback is 30 days.
claims.quote: The maximum lookback is 30 days from the current date.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Microsoft identifies the documented DSPM as classic and says a new version has replaced it.
claims.quote: This article is for the classic version of Data Security Posture Management, now replaced with a new version

claims.claim: Microsoft says the new version's improvements will not be added to DSPM (classic).
claims.quote: These improvements won't be added to this classic version

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: DSPM Copilot supports asking for sensitive data activities of a named user.
claims.quote: Show all sensitive data activities performed by <upn> in the last <duration> days

claims.claim: DSPM Copilot supports asking about a named user's potential sensitive data exfiltration.
claims.quote: Was <upn> involved in any potential sensitive data exfiltration (for example, email forwarding, external file sharing, USB transfers, cloud uploads) in the last <duration> days?

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: DSPM Copilot supports asking for a named user's alerts and current risk level.
claims.quote: Are there any alerts associated with <upn> in the last <duration> days, and what is the user's current risk level?

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The Data Security Viewer role is required to use Security Copilot in DSPM.
claims.quote: Data Security Viewer role. If the DSPM dashboard is opted in, this role grants permission to view all the insights. This role is required to use Security Copilot in DSPM.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Access to the Security Copilot platform requires a Security Copilot owner or contributor assignment.
claims.quote: Specific Security Copilot roles must be assigned in order for a group or individual to access the Security Copilot platform. ... Security Copilot owner; Security Copilot contributor

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Security Copilot uses on-behalf-of authentication to access security data through active Microsoft plugins.
claims.quote: Copilot uses on-behalf-of authentication to access security-related data through active Microsoft plugins.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Running these prompts does not expand the user's underlying access to security data.
claims.quote: Security Copilot doesn't go beyond the access you have ... Each Microsoft plugin has its own role requirements that remain in effect to access the plugin's service and its data.

claims.claim: Security Copilot roles grant platform access but do not themselves grant access to security data.
claims.quote: Instead, they only control access to the capabilities of the Security Copilot platform and provide no access by themselves to security data.

claims.claim: Recommended Microsoft Security roles is the default contributor assignment for new Security Copilot instances.
claims.quote: The assignment of the recommended Microsoft security roles to Copilot is the default for new Security Copilot instances.

claims.claim: Some existing tenants retain the former Everyone contributor assignment.
claims.quote: Existing customers who have the everyone group assigned may continue to use the assignment.

claims.claim: Several Purview roles automatically inherit Security Copilot owner access.
claims.quote: The following ... Microsoft Purview roles automatically inherit Copilot owner access ... Purview Compliance Administrator; Purview Data Governance Administrator; Purview Organization Management

claims.claim: Groups assigned Security Copilot permissions must be role-assignable groups.
claims.quote: Security Copilot only supports assigning permissions to Role-assignable groups.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: DSPM (classic) requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft Purview Suite.
claims.quote: To access and use DSPM, you need a Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance) license.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Suite was formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance)

claims.claim: The organization must be configured for Security Copilot to use it in DSPM.
claims.quote: To access Copilot in DSPM, you must configure your organization for Security Copilot.

claims.claim: DSPM analytics processing must be opted in.
claims.quote: Step 2: Opt in to analytics processing and scanning

claims.claim: The automated scan must complete before using the featured promptbooks and gallery.
claims.quote: After you configure DSPM, onboard your organization to Security Copilot, and complete the automated scanning, use Security Copilot featured promptbooks and the new prompt gallery to help you get started.

claims.claim: Users whose permissions are restricted to specific administrative units cannot access DSPM.
claims.quote: If your permissions are restricted in specific administrative units in your organization, you can't access DSPM.

claims.claim: Opting in to DSPM automatically enables Insider Risk Management and DLP analytics if not already active.
claims.quote: When you opt into DSPM, the system automatically enables analytics in Insider Risk Management and analytics in DLP if they're not already active.

claims.claim: Initial scanning and processing can take up to three days.
claims.quote: When you complete the opt-in process, the system starts an automated scan ... It might take up to three days for this processing to complete.

claims.where: summary; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Running gallery prompts consumes Security Compute Units because DSPM is an embedded Security Copilot experience.
claims.quote: You consume SCUs in the following scenarios: ... Running embedded Security Copilot experiences

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining DSPM subscription entitlement with Security Copilot capacity.
claims.quote: To access and use DSPM, you need a Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft Purview Suite ... license. ... To access Copilot in DSPM, you must configure your organization for Security Copilot.

claims.claim: Variable is consistent with the published SCU consumption meter and provisioned/overage billing.
claims.quote: Provisioned capacity is billed by the hour while the overage capacity is billed on usage.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Eligible Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 customers receive automatically provisioned Security Copilot capacity once their tenant is enabled.
claims.quote: If Security Copilot is included in your Microsoft 365 E5 or E7 license and your tenant has been enabled, Microsoft will automatically provision and onboard

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Customers without Security Copilot inclusion must provision SCUs.
claims.quote: Non-Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 customers ... You must provision this capacity before you can use Security Copilot.

claims.claim: Provisioned capacity has a minimum of one SCU.
claims.quote: SCUs are provisioned in advance (minimum of one SCU)

claims.claim: Provisioned SCUs are billed per hour.
claims.quote: Provisioned capacity is billed per hour and is best for steady, predictable usage.

claims.claim: Overage SCUs are billed on actual usage.
claims.quote: Provisioned capacity is billed by the hour while the overage capacity is billed on usage.

claims.claim: Overage SCU billing uses one decimal place rather than rounding up to whole SCUs.
claims.quote: Consumed units aren't rounded up to whole numbers. This means that you're charged precisely based on your usage (to one decimal place).

claims.claim: Generally available capabilities are charged under the published SCU charging table.
claims.quote: Capability stage | Charged? ... Generally available (GA) | Yes

claims.claim: Public preview capabilities are charged under the published SCU charging table.
claims.quote: Capability stage | Charged? ... Public preview | Yes

claims.claim: Overage capacity can have a maximum limit or be unlimited.
claims.quote: Overage units are billed on-demand and can be set as unlimited or a maximum amount.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing: Cap
claims.claim: When provisioned and overage capacity is exhausted, prompt submission stops until more capacity becomes available in the next hour.
claims.quote: When the provisioned and overage SCUs is crossed ... Analysts can't submit more prompts at this time. More capacity would become available in the next hour.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs readers to its Security Copilot pricing page for SCU pricing.
claims.quote: For more information, see Microsoft Security Copilot pricing and the Pricing calculator page.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Not yet published; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a fixed SCU figure for the gallery's prompts; the capacity page gives worked examples.
claims.quote: Searched: DSPM Copilot prompt gallery Security Compute Units cost per prompt. Read DSPM Copilot, security-compute-units-capacity and faq-security-copilot; examples are not gallery rates, and the FAQ says consumption varies with prompt complexity.

claims.where: Why it matters: Every prompt and promptbook run is billed in SCUs
claims.claim: Every prompt and promptbook run is billed in SCUs.
claims.quote: Provisioned capacity is billed by the hour while the overage capacity is billed on usage. ... Runs a prompt | 3.0 SCUs ... Runs a promptbook | 3.7 SCUs
claims.fix: Replace with 'Every prompt and promptbook run consumes SCUs.' Add 'For enabled Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 inclusion tenants, usage deducts from included monthly capacity rather than generating hourly capacity charges.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/security/security-copilot-inclusion, which says the default capacity 'isn't billed hourly' and its UI cost values are 'informational only, not charges'.

claims.claim: No separate UI or API switch to show or hide the DSPM prompt gallery is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: DSPM Copilot prompt gallery disable enable setting PowerShell API; "DSPM" "prompt gallery" "switch"; "DSPM" "prompt gallery" "disable". Read DSPM Copilot, DSPM get-started and Security Copilot owner-settings; found no gallery-specific switch.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The gallery is user-opt-in: qualifying analysts choose a prompt and run it.
claims.quote: To view these built-in Copilot prompts, select View more in prompt gallery ... You can customize the built-in prompt or immediately run the prompt directly in Copilot.

claims.claim: Purview role-group membership is managed through Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. ... On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group ... Select Edit ... On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to a role group and grants the group's effective role permissions.
claims.quote: When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group. ... -Identity ... role group ... -Member ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: The documented Purview role-group editing procedure uses an administrator assigned Role management.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal by using credentials for an admin account assigned the Role management role.

claims.claim: Data Security Viewers is a role group associated with the Data Security Viewer role.
claims.quote: Data Security Viewers role group and Data Security Viewer role ... View Security Copilot insights and run prompts ... additional role groups required ... Data Security Viewers

claims.claim: Security Copilot role assignment is reached through Home menu > Owner > Role assignment > Add members.
claims.quote: Select the home menu. Select Role assignment > Add members. ... Select the person or group. Select the Security Copilot role to assign (Copilot owner or Copilot contributor).
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Home menu > Owner > Role assignment > Add members > Copilot owner or Copilot contributor'. The current route reaches the correct dialog but stops before choosing the role; the cited Navigate Security Copilot page supplies the Owner menu step.

claims.claim: No direct API or PowerShell operation assigning the Security Copilot owner or contributor role is documented in the references searched.
claims.quote: Searched: Security Copilot role assignment API Microsoft Graph workspace owners contributors; "Security Copilot" "role assignments" "API" Graph update workspace. Read authentication, Graph workspace reference and Update-MgBetaSecurityCopilotWorkspace; no role-assignment operation.

claims.claim: Preinstalled plugin availability is controlled at Owner > Plugin settings > preinstalled plugin > All users or Owners only.
claims.quote: On the left navigation, navigate to Owner. Select Plugin settings. ... Choose to manage preinstalled plugin availability and restrict access. ... two options for plugin availability: All users; Owners only

claims.claim: No operation setting the preinstalled-plugin All users versus Owners only restriction is documented in the references searched.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Security Copilot preinstalled plugin restrictions API PowerShell owners only. Read manage-plugins, Graph plugin reference and New-MgBetaSecurityCopilotWorkspacePlugin; no documented owner-only restriction property or operation.

claims.claim: Only Security Copilot owners can change availability of preinstalled plugins.
claims.quote: Change availability of preinstalled plugins for the tenant | Copilot owner: Yes | Copilot contributor: No

claims.claim: Restricting preinstalled-plugin access takes effect immediately.
claims.quote: Restricting access is an immediate change impacting all users of Security Copilot and embedded experiences.

claims.claim: Preinstalled-plugin availability restrictions apply to standalone and embedded Security Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: You can choose to make specific plugins accessible to everyone or restrict them to owners only. These settings apply to both standalone and embedded Security Copilot experiences.

claims.claim: Overage capacity can be changed through Home menu > Owner > Owner settings > Number of overage units > Change.
claims.quote: Through the owner settings page: Under Security compute units or Number of overage units, select Change.

claims.claim: An API or CLI operation setting the maximum overage SCUs is not documented in the references searched.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft SecurityCopilot capacities update overageUnits REST API; Microsoft.SecurityCopilot/capacities capacity resource properties overage; Security Copilot overage capacity az resource update REST. Read manage-usage, owner-settings and capacity documentation; no setting operation.

claims.claim: Changing capacity in the Security Copilot portal requires both Azure capacity owner or contributor rights and Security Copilot owner rights.
claims.quote: Security Copilot portal required role: Azure capacity owner or contributor who are also Security Copilot owners.

claims.claim: Provisioned and overage SCUs can also be updated in the Azure portal.
claims.quote: You can update provisioned security compute units and overage units in the Azure portal and the Security Copilot portal.

claims.claim: The usage documentation gives Home menu > Owner settings > Usage monitoring as the dashboard route.
claims.quote: Sign in to Security Copilot ... and go to the Home menu > Owner settings. Select Usage monitoring.

claims.claim: An API returning the dashboard's SCU consumption by user, plugin and experience is not documented in the references searched.
claims.quote: Searched: Security Copilot usage monitoring API SCU consumption export; "Security Copilot" "usage" "Graph" "reports". Read manage-usage, Graph workspace reference and activity-export-api; exports cover prompts/evaluations, not the dashboard's SCU breakdown.

claims.claim: Copilot owners can view the usage monitoring dashboard.
claims.quote: Copilot owners can view the usage over time within the Microsoft Security Copilot usage monitoring dashboard.

claims.claim: The dashboard includes up to 90 days of data.
claims.quote: The dashboard includes up to 90 days of data, offering a robust window into recent activity.

claims.claim: Usage dashboard data can be exported to Excel.
claims.quote: Export usage dashboard data into Excel files for easier analysis, sharing, or offline access.

claims.claim: Usage data can be broken down by user, plugin, Copilot experience and category, including promptbook sessions.
claims.quote: The following filters are available: Copilot experience; Users; Plugins used; Type; Category ... Promptbook: A session related to a promptbook.

claims.claim: The navigation article instead lists Usage monitoring alongside Owner settings under the Owner menu, which is visible only to owners.
claims.quote: Owner - This menu is available only if you have the Security Copilot Owner role. ... Owner settings ... Plugin settings ... Role assignment ... Usage monitoring

claims.claim: The logging toggle is at Home menu > Owner > Owner settings > Logging audit data in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Select the home menu icon. Navigate to the Owner > Owner settings > Logging audit data in Microsoft Purview. ... You can turn the toggle on or off.

claims.claim: An API or PowerShell equivalent for the Security Copilot Logging audit data in Microsoft Purview toggle is not documented in the references searched.
claims.quote: Searched: Security Copilot Logging audit data in Microsoft Purview settings API PowerShell; "Security Copilot" "audit" "PowerShell" "enable". Read audit-log, owner-settings and Graph workspace reference; no operation setting the Copilot logging toggle.

claims.claim: A Security Administrator can configure the Security Copilot audit logging option.
claims.quote: A Security Administrator can also access this option through the Owner settings page.

claims.where: controls[6].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Security Copilot must allow Purview access for its activity to be available through the unified audit log.
claims.quote: To enable Purview DSPM for AI and UAL solutions for Security Copilot, the capability must be enabled within Security Copilot and configured within the respective Purview solutions.

claims.claim: For Purview auditing of Security Copilot, prompt and response content is included only through DSPM for AI.
claims.quote: Customer content such as that contained within the prompt and response pair is currently only included through Microsoft Purview DSPM for AI.

claims.claim: The sources do not describe the DSPM promptbooks as applying the policy changes they suggest.
claims.quote: Searched: "DSPM" "promptbooks" "apply" "policies". Read DSPM Copilot and DSPM get-started; promptbooks suggest policy changes, while taking action on recommendations is documented separately. No automatic application by these promptbooks was found.

claims.claim: Security Copilot capacity-limit notifications also apply in embedded experiences such as DSPM.
claims.quote: The capacity limit notifications are also shown in Security Copilot embedded experiences and it informs the analyst to contact the Azure capacity owner or contributor to increase the capacity or limit the number of prompts to avoid disruptions.
